units.zh: 德勸垂乘釁討堅，辭旨慷慨，識者言其有遠略，垂竟不能用。
units.en: Murong De urged Murong Chui to strike Fu Jian while Qin was divided, speaking with such fire that men of judgment called him far-sighted—yet Murong Chui would not act.
units.literal: De urged Chui to exploit the opening to punish Jian; his words were fervent; observers said he had long-range strategy; Chui in the end could not employ it.

units.zh: 德兄垂甚壯之，因共論軍國大謀，言必切至。
units.en: Murong Chui, impressed, began debating statecraft and strategy with him, and Murong De’s advice was always blunt and to the point.
units.literal: De’s elder brother Chui greatly admired him; therefore they together discussed great plans of army and state; his words were always incisive and to the point.

units.zh: 垂謂之曰：「汝器識長進，非復吳下阿蒙也。」
units.en: Chui said to him: “Your capacity and insight have advanced; you are no longer the young Meng east of Wu.”
units.literal: Chui said to him: “Your capacity and insight have advanced; you are no longer the young Meng east of Wu.”

units.zh: 枋頭之役，德以征南將軍與垂擊敗晉師。
units.en: At the battle of Fangtou he joined Murong Chui as general who campaigns south and helped shatter the Eastern Jin army.
units.literal: In the Fangtou campaign, De as general who campaigns south together with Chui struck and defeated Jin troops.

units.en: When Murong Chui defected to Fu Jian, Murong De lost his post as an accomplice.
units.literal: When Chui fled to Fu Jian, De sat fault and was dismissed from office.

units.zh: 後遇垂敗，徙于長安，苻堅以為張掖太守，數歲免歸。
units.en: After Murong Chui’s defeat he was moved to Chang’an, where Fu Jian named him prefect of Zhangye; a few years later he was dismissed and sent home.
units.literal: Later encountering Chui’s defeat, he was moved to Chang’an; Fu Jian appointed him prefect of Zhangye; after several years he was dismissed and returned.

units.zh: 及堅以兵臨江，拜德為奮威將軍。
units.en: When Fu Jian marched his host to the great river, he named Murong De general who rouses might.
units.literal: When Jian led troops to the Yangzi, he appointed De general who rouses might.

units.zh: 堅之敗也，堅與張夫人相失，慕容垂將護致之，德正色謂垂曰：「昔楚莊滅陳，納巫臣之諫而棄夏姬。
units.en: When Jian was defeated, he and Consort Zhang lost each other. Murong Chui was about to escort her back, but De, with a stern expression, said to Chui: “When King Zhuang of Chu destroyed Chen, he accepted Wu Chen’s remonstrance and cast aside Xia Ji.
units.literal: When Jian was defeated, he and Consort Zhang lost each other. Murong Chui was about to escort her back, but De, with a stern expression, said to Chui: “When King Zhuang of Chu destroyed Chen, he accepted Wu Chen’s remonstrance and cast aside Xia Ji.

units.zh: 此不祥之人，惑亂人主，戎事不邇女器，秦之敗師當由於此。
units.en: This is an inauspicious woman who deludes and disorders rulers. In military affairs one does not bring women near; Qin’s defeat in battle must have come from this.
units.literal: This is an inauspicious woman who deludes and disorders rulers. In military affairs one does not bring women near; Qin’s defeat in battle must have come from this.

units.zh: 宜掩目而過，奈何將衛之也！」
units.en: You should cover your eyes and pass her by—how can you intend to escort and protect her!”
units.literal: You should cover your eyes and pass her by—how can you intend to escort and protect her!”

units.zh: 雅之等頓首答曰：「幸蒙陛下天覆之恩，大造之澤，存亡繼絕，實在聖時，雖則萬隕，何以上報！」
units.en: Yazhi and the others bowed their heads to the ground and replied: “We have fortunately received Your Majesty’s heaven-covering grace and great creative favor, preserving the dying and continuing the cut off. Truly this lies in a sage age; even if we fell ten thousand times, how could we repay it above!”
units.literal: Yazhi and the others bowed their heads to the ground and replied: “We have fortunately received Your Majesty’s heaven-covering grace and great creative favor, preserving the dying and continuing the cut off. Truly this lies in a sage age; even if we fell ten thousand times, how could we repay it above!”

units.zh: 俄聞桓玄敗，德以慕容鎮為前鋒，慕容鐘為大都督，配以步卒二萬，騎五千，克期將發，而德寢疾，於是罷兵。
units.en: Soon they heard Huan Xuan was defeated; Murong De made Murong Zhen the vanguard and Murong Zhong supreme commander, assigning twenty thousand foot and five thousand horse with a set departure date, but Murong De fell ill and therefore halted the army.
units.literal: Soon they heard Huan Xuan was defeated; De made Murong Zhen vanguard and Murong Zhong supreme commander, pairing them with twenty thousand foot and five thousand horse, fixing a date to set out, but De took to bed ill, and therefore the army was halted.

units.zh: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。
units.en: Murong Chao, whom he had summoned from Chang'an, now arrived.
units.literal: Earlier, De had welcomed his brother's son Chao from Chang'an; at this point he arrived.

units.zh: 德夜夢其父曰：「汝既無子，何不早立超為太子，不爾，惡人生心。」
units.en: De dreamed at night his father said, 'You have no son; why not early establish Chao as crown prince—otherwise evil men will breed designs.'
units.literal: De dreamed at night his father said, 'You have no son; why not early establish Chao as crown prince—otherwise evil men will breed designs.'

units.zh: 寐而告其妻曰：「先帝神明所敕，觀此夢意，吾將死矣。」
units.en: Awake he told his wife, 'The late emperor's spirit commanded; looking at this dream's meaning, I am about to die.'
units.literal: Awake he told his wife, 'The late emperor's spirit commanded; looking at this dream's meaning, I am about to die.'

units.zh: 乃下書以超為皇太子，大赦境內，子為父後者人爵二級。
units.en: He named Murong Chao crown prince and issued a broad amnesty.
units.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict making Chao crown prince, amnestied the realm, and for sons continuing fathers raised each man's rank two grades.

units.zh: 其月死，即義熙元年也，時年七十。
units.en: He died the same month, in the first year of Yixi, at seventy sui.
units.literal: That month he died; it was the first year of Yixi, and at the time his age was seventy sui.

proposals.before: Chui said to him: “Your capacity and insight have advanced; you are no longer the young Meng east of Wu.”
proposals.after: Chui said to him: “Your capacity and insight have advanced; you are no longer Ah Meng of Wu.”
proposals.reason: 吳下阿蒙 is a nickname/allusive expression for Ah Meng of Wu. The current east of Wu is not in the source; young also obscures 阿蒙 as the name. Preserve the complete quotation.

proposals.reason: The source explicitly says 德...其兄子超: Chao is De’s elder brother’s son. Restore that omitted relationship and preserve his arrival after the earlier summons.

proposals.after: Murong De’s elder brother Murong Chui was greatly impressed and began debating statecraft and strategy with him, and Murong De’s advice was always blunt and to the point.
proposals.reason: 德兄垂 explicitly calls Chui De’s elder brother, as the literal field already says (De’s elder brother Chui). The idiomatic field drops this kinship. I also checked the elder-brother wording in s0272. 甚壯之 means he greatly admired him.

proposals.before: When Murong Chui defected to Fu Jian, Murong De lost his post as an accomplice.
proposals.after: When Murong Chui defected to Fu Jian, Murong De was implicated and dismissed from office.
proposals.reason: 坐免職 means De was dismissed because he was implicated in Chui’s flight (坐, liability by association). As an accomplice says he took part, which the source does not say. The literal (sat fault and was dismissed) is a calque without that claim, so I leave it.

proposals.before: He named Murong Chao crown prince and issued a broad amnesty.
proposals.after: He issued an edict naming Murong Chao crown prince, proclaimed a general amnesty within his realm, and raised by two degrees the rank of every son who was his father’s heir.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic field leaves out 子為父後者人爵二級, a concrete grant in the same edict that the literal field keeps. 下書 (issued an edict) and 境內 (within the realm) are also restored. No date or person is added.

proposals.before: When Chui fled to Fu Jian, De sat fault and was dismissed from office.
proposals.after: When Chui fled to Fu Jian, De was implicated and dismissed from office.
proposals.reason: The literal calque sat fault does not convey the legal implication expressed by 坐免職. Restore the proposition that De was implicated and dismissed, preserving Chui’s flight and naming no new event participant.

decisions.reason: 吳下 means in Wu, the region of Wu, not east of Wu. 阿蒙 is the familiar name Ah Meng, which young Meng hides. This is Lu Su’s proverbial jibe at Lü Meng, quoted by Chui. Ah Meng of Wu is faithful, keeps the whole quotation and identifies no one new.
The literal field had the same east-of-Wu and young-Meng mistranslation, word for word. Ah Meng of Wu renders 吳下阿蒙 exactly, so both fields now read the same way.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 汝器識長進，非復吳下阿蒙也

decisions.reason: 其兄子超 explicitly makes Chao the son of De’s elder brother (兄), and the idiomatic field had dropped this. Had summoned keeps the earlier act marked by 初 separate from 及是而至, the arrival now. It adds no date, name or identity for the father.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至

decisions.reason: 兄 means elder brother, so his brother’s son was too vague. 迎 here is De’s earlier act of sending for or fetching Chao from Chang’an, which Later Qin held. Welcomed wrongly suggests a reception at the arrival, which came later (及是而至). Summoned is acceptable and keeps the two stages apart.

references.title: Zizhi Tongjian066, Lü Meng study anecdote, under Jianan15
references.quote: 初，權謂呂蒙曰：「卿今當塗掌事，不可不學。」蒙辭以軍中多務。權曰：「孤豈欲卿治經為博士邪！但當涉獵，見往事耳。卿言多務，孰若孤！孤常讀書，自以為大有所益。」蒙乃始就學。及魯肅過尋陽，與蒙論議，大驚曰：「卿今者才略，非復吳下阿蒙！」蒙曰：「士別三日，即更刮目相待，大兄何見事之晚乎！」肅遂拜蒙母，結友而別。
references.reason: Primary narrative confirms Ah Meng is Lü Meng’s nickname in a retrospective learning anecdote; the chapter127 allusion does not itself date his living activity AD200–219. This is not a new chapter127 date assignment.
